Session 4: Descriptive and exploratory network analysis

Describing the whole network, positions within it, and groups

Published

October 4, 2026

Goals

  • describe a network at three levels: whole network, nodes, groups,
  • understand what each centrality measure actually counts,
  • detect communities and test for homophily,
  • visualise networks so the picture supports, rather than replaces, the analysis.
library(tidyverse)
library(igraph)
library(tidygraph)
library(ggraph)

We practise on a small, well-known network before moving to IR data. 

g <- make_graph("Zachary")
plot(g, vertex.size = 8, vertex.label.cex = 0.7)

1. Whole-network level

NoteThink first

For each measure below, write down in one sentence what it counts before you run the code.

tibble(
  nodes        = vcount(g),
  edges        = ecount(g),
  density      = edge_density(g),
  components   = components(g)$no,
  transitivity = transitivity(g, type = "global"),
  avg_path     = mean_distance(g),
  diameter     = diameter(g)
)
# A tibble: 1 × 7
  nodes edges density components transitivity avg_path diameter
  <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl>      <dbl>        <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>
1    34    78   0.139          1        0.256     2.41        5

Degree distribution: are ties spread evenly or concentrated on a few nodes?

tibble(degree = degree(g)) |>
  ggplot(aes(degree)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(x = "Degree", y = "Number of nodes")

2. Node level: centrality

Different centrality measures formalise different ideas of importance:

Measure Idea IR intuition
Degree how many ties number of trade partners
Betweenness how often on shortest paths between others broker, gatekeeper
Closeness how close to everyone else reach, speed of diffusion
Eigenvector tied to well-connected others ties to great powers 
centralities <- tibble(
  node        = 1:vcount(g),
  degree      = degree(g),
  betweenness = betweenness(g),
  closeness   = closeness(g),
  eigenvector = eigen_centrality(g)$vector
)

centralities |> arrange(desc(betweenness)) |> head()

3. Group level: communities and homophily

comm <- cluster_louvain(g)
sizes(comm)
Community sizes
 1  2  3  4 
12  5 11  6 
modularity(comm)
[1] 0.4188034

Homophily (assortativity): do similar nodes tie to each other? Here we use degree: do well-connected nodes connect to other well-connected nodes?

assortativity_degree(g)
[1] -0.4756131

With a node attribute such as regime type, assortativity_nominal() asks whether democracies tie to democracies.

4. Visualisation with ggraph

g |>
  as_tbl_graph() |>
  activate(nodes) |>
  mutate(
    betweenness = centrality_betweenness(),
    community   = as.factor(group_louvain())
  ) |>
  ggraph(layout = "fr") +
  geom_edge_link(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_node_point(aes(size = betweenness, colour = community)) +
  theme_void()
WarningDiscuss

Re-run the plot several times. The layout changes, the network does not. What can and cannot be read from a network plot?
